kel.heroSubtitle: Medical Management of Raised & Overgrown Scars
kel.heroDesc1: Keloids are abnormal scars that grow beyond the original wound boundary and may continue to enlarge over time. They can cause cosmetic concern, itching, pain, or tightness and often require medical treatment rather than home remedies.
kel.heroDesc2: In Malaysia, keloid treatment must be performed by licensed medical practitioners in regulated medical facilities. Treatments involve prescription medications and medical procedures governed by international regulatory standards, including guidance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on injectable medications used in scar management.
kel.whatDesc1: A keloid is a type of abnormal scar caused by excessive collagen production during wound healing. Major clinical institutions such as the Mayo Clinic describe keloids as benign but persistent scars that often require professional treatment to control symptoms and appearance.
kel.whatDesc2: Unlike normal scars, keloids have distinct characteristics that make them challenging to manage without medical intervention.
kel.char2: Do not regress on their own
kel.char3: May continue to grow over time
kel.areasDesc: Keloids commonly develop on specific body areas. They are more common in individuals with darker skin types and may have a genetic predisposition.
kel.whyDesc1: Keloids do not respond well to topical creams or massage alone. Evidence-based reviews indexed by NCBI / PubMed show that keloids have a high recurrence rate and often require combination therapy for optimal control.
kel.treatmentDesc: Treatment is individualised and may include one or more of the following approaches. According to clinical guidance summarised by MedlinePlus (NIH), combination approaches are often necessary due to the recurrent nature of keloids.
kel.safetyDesc: Keloid treatment is generally safe when performed by trained medical professionals. Possible temporary effects depend on the method used.
kel.timeline2: Multiple treatment sessions are usually required
kel.timeline3: Flattening and symptom relief often occur over weeks to months
kel.timeline4: Maintenance or repeat treatments may be necessary
kel.importantNoteDesc: No treatment guarantees zero recurrence. Long-term monitoring is often required.
kel.candidateDesc: Keloid treatment may be suitable for individuals who meet the following criteria. A medical assessment is essential to confirm diagnosis and choose the appropriate approach.
kel.candidate5: Are willing to follow a long-term treatment plan

kel.faqDesc: Get answers to common concerns about keloid treatment
kel.faq1A: Keloids result from excessive collagen production during wound healing.
kel.faq2A: No. Keloids are benign, but they can cause discomfort and cosmetic concerns.
kel.faq3Q: Can keloids go away on their own?
kel.faq3A: No. Keloids typically persist and may grow without medical treatment.
kel.faq4Q: What is the most effective keloid treatment?
kel.faq4A: Steroid injections are commonly first-line, often combined with other therapies.
kel.faq5A: Most patients require multiple sessions over several months.
kel.faq6Q: Do keloids come back after treatment?
kel.faq6A: Recurrence is possible, which is why combination therapy and follow-up are important.
kel.faq7A: Discomfort is usually mild and well tolerated.
kel.faq8A: Patients with active infections or certain medical conditions may need to delay treatment.
kel.ref1Desc: FDA guidance on injectable corticosteroids used in scar management treatments.
kel.ref2Desc: Clinical overview describing keloids as benign but persistent scars requiring professional treatment.
kel.ref3Desc: Evidence-based reviews showing high recurrence rates and need for combination therapy.
kel.ctaTitle: Take control of your keloid treatment.
kel.ctaDesc: Keloids require medical strategy, patience, and long-term planning. With evidence-based treatment and proper follow-up, symptoms can be controlled and scar appearance significantly improved—while respecting the biology of scar formation.
